test_policy.notes: First-time freshmen must provide an ACT or SAT result (valid within 5 years); the page states no score alone guarantees admission and scores are used with other factors. The CDS adds that scores are required unless waived by a particularly strong high school GPA. The international requirements page lists high school GPA and English proficiency as the primary factors and does not mention SAT/ACT, so confirm with admissions@memphis.edu whether an international applicant can be reviewed without scores.

requirements.notes: International undergraduate application fee $50 ($25 for domestic freshmen). The UofM now accepts the Common App from first-time freshmen. International applicants upload their transcript or marks sheet to the portal (official copy needed before enrollment); decisions typically come within 5-7 business days. Self-reported GPA and test scores are accepted at application. Minimum high school units: English 4, math 3, science 2, social studies 2 (incl. U.S. History), foreign language 2, visual/performing arts 1. Nursing (BSN) has its own application deadlines.

deadlines.label: Scholarship consideration priority deadline (admitted students)
deadlines.notes: The page strongly encourages applying before Nov. 1 for scholarship eligibility; international scholarships also use the Dec. 1 priority date (freshmen). Updated GPA and test scores can be submitted through March.

deadlines.label: International applicants outside the U.S. (first-time F-1): fall 2027 application deadline
deadlines.notes: File completion deadline July 15. Spring: Nov. 1 (file complete Dec. 1). Admission is rolling and space-available. Printed without a year, treated as fall 2027.

deadlines.label: International applicants already in the U.S.: fall 2027 application and file completion deadline

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required of all international students unless they are citizens of an English-speaking country whose native language is English or were taught in English in high school or college. Alternatives to a test: SAT EBRW 540+, ACT English 21+, IB Higher Level English A1 grade 5, GED 450 / HiSET 45, Cambridge GCE/GCSE/IGCSE English B or higher, one semester of U.S. English Composition with C or better, high school graduation in the U.S. or an approved English-speaking country with 2+ years of enrollment, a medium-of-instruction letter (committee discretion), or the Prep Academy. Tests must be within two years. Students below the minimum can join the Intensive English for Internationals (IEI) program (iei@memphis.edu) to gain certification and full admission.

english.notes: Tests taken after 2025 (1-6 scale). The page lists '61 Prior to 2026 / 4 after 2025'.

aid.notes: Competitive merit scholarships go to newly admitted degree-seeking F-1/J-1 international students (dual citizens and permanent residents are not eligible). Two paths: GPA plus ACT/SAT, or GPA only for certain awards. Renewable for up to three more years with 12+ credit hours, good standing and service hours. Freshmen should apply by Dec. 1 for priority. Award amounts are not given in the page text. CDS H6: 165 nonresident undergraduates received institutional aid, average $18,732 (the CDS does not say whether it was need- or non-need-based).

sat.note: The reviewed Memphis pages do not print a numeric SAT code; look it up in the College Board code search.

act.note: The reviewed Memphis pages do not print a numeric ACT code; look it up at act.org.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is printed; official scores must be sent directly to the University of Memphis.
